A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same UnMaskFork research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original coding and MATH evaluations, scaling curves, caching and action-set ablations, and a generation case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original block-diffusion, three-model, runtime/memory, verifier-robustness, and baseline-comparison results.

M1.justification: The main MCTS algorithm, deterministic actions, and caching remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds a targeted block-diffusion adaptation: actions remain fixed within each block, and search-node creation at mask-ratio checkpoints is deferred until the block boundary.

E1.justification: LiveCodeBench, HumanEval+, MBPP+, and MATH remain the datasets and tasks. Appendix A.5 adds an incomplete-verifier scenario in which search receives reduced public-test feedback while evaluation still uses private tests. The additional model configurations do not introduce new task domains.

E2.justification: ReMDM and TReASURe, previously discussed only as related work, are now evaluated against UMF on LiveCodeBench and MATH respectively (Tables 12–13). This substantially extends direct comparison, including adding a MATH comparator where v1 reported UMF alone. Existing BoN, DTS*, Pair, and AB-MCTS comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include block-size-4 decoding, a three-model configuration at fixed NFE, public-test dropping, and runtime/memory measurement. Appendix A.6 also compares rule-based extraction and math_verify on identical MATH outputs. The retained main experiments keep their sample sizes and budgets; identifying math_verify for unchanged main scores does not establish that their evaluation procedure changed.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis beyond the original caching, action-type, and two-model ablations. It adds tokenizer-length drift measurement, three-model action-set analysis, runtime/memory and offloading analysis, public-test dropout robustness, and answer-extraction sensitivity. Table 3 also supplements cache-hit rates with saved-NFE measurements.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without documented repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original main benchmark scores are retained, but substantial results are added. Tables 5 and 7 report three-model scores of 32/87/76 alongside unchanged two-model scores of 28/88/72. Table 6 reports block-decoding scores rising from 19% to 31% across budgets, and Table 10 reports 28/28/25/24% under increasing public-test dropout. Other additions include runtime/memory, alternative MATH extraction, and ReMDM/TReASURe results. These are additional configurations and evaluations, not revised scores for the original setting.

T1.justification: The formal state/action definitions, kernel-selection inequality in Equation (1), rollout-variance reasoning, and Appendix B remasking definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about deterministic branching, cached MCTS, and coding/mathematical reasoning performance. The additional experiments expand support without redefining the announced contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: it replaces the exclusionary rationale for block diffusion with demonstrated compatibility, discusses memory-constrained deployment and incomplete-verifier robustness, and adds hypotheses about localized remasking and noisy intermediate-state rewards. Appendix A.7 explicitly qualifies the new comparisons because search formulations and reward interfaces differ.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies existing tokenizer conversion and the fixed generation window, and identifies math_verify for the retained MATH scores. New reproducibility information includes block size 4, additional model identities, single-H100 hardware for coding runtime measurements, GPU residency and CPU-offloading guidance, model memory and transfer times, and PRM invocation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Stable-DiffCoder citation and removes the Arriola et al. block-diffusion reference. Appendix A.7 adds focused positioning against ReMDM and TReASURe, while the main related-work narrative remains stable. The PG-DLM title/year update refers to the same cited work.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify tokenizer handling, evaluation, and ablation interpretation; subsection capitalization is standardized. Appendix A is organized into A.1–A.7, but the main narrative and section order remain largely intact. The added scientific material does not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 6–13 substantially expand the presentation of compatibility, efficiency, robustness, verification, and comparator evidence, with some retained results redisplayed for comparison. Tables 3 and 5 gain information and expanded captions/structure. The existing case-study graphics are brought together and swap Figure 3/4 numbering; the original scaling plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's predominantly NFE-based validation by measuring actual runtime and memory, testing sensitivity to verifier availability and answer extraction, and demonstrating block-decoding compatibility. These additions materially strengthen assessment of practical efficiency and applicability while preserving the original evidence. The new baseline comparisons are explicitly qualified, although their configurations remain incompletely documented and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
